summary:
COSMIC EYE is an interactive astronomical analysis tool for the study of the time evolution of celestial bodies and regions of space. The platform taps into publicly available observations from NASA’s SPHEREx archive, to access and organize astronomical images by different observation dates, enabling users to compare the same region over time.

COSMIC EYE provides tools for chronological observation timelines, image comparison, brightness measurements, positional analysis and difference maps. It also attempts to translate scientific measurements into understandable explanations using AI, while taking into account image noise, calibration differences, instrumental artifacts, and measurement uncertainty.

COSMIC EYE integrates astronomical archival data, image processing and accessible scientific visualization for a simpler exploration, understanding and investigation of temporal astronomical analysis.
details:
A platform which can help analyse astronomical data and provide a better understanding of changes in celestial objects/areas.

This has been developed using free astronomical data from the NASA SPHEREx archive. The user can search for celestial objects and/or coordinates and view any observations. The observations have been ordered by date so they can be compared. The user can see how bright the object is, where it is located and how intense the image is. New and mobile objects can be seen.

This platform allows the user to analyse astronomical data. It allows them to measure brightness, compare location, produce difference maps and view when the observations were taken. The results have been explained using AI. The noise, artifacts, calibration, background and uncertainties have been considered to ensure the differences in images are not misleading.

This platform offers an easy way to view astronomical data in archives. It will help users understand and view the changes in data. This will aid learning within Astronomy, encourage scientific discovery and provide a simple starting point to understand how the universe changes.

This was developed using React.js, JavaScript, HTML5 and CSS3. Methods to retrieve astronomical data, process images and consider how AI can be used.

This platform is creative as it considers how observations can be connected over time. By ordering the data by date, comparing visually, measuring scientifically and explaining using AI we are aiming to make a more integrated platform.

We have considered using scientific, reliable data with good quality images. We have also considered how important it is to know that changes in the images are actual changes in the universe. We want to provide real data and ensure our conclusions are backed up by science.
